text: At the 79th minute, Westport Albion deliberately reduced their pressing intensity (PPDA rising from 4.2 to 6.2) and lowered their defensive line height by 0.25 while slowing tempo by 0.35 to protect a 3-2 lead. This tactical shift transitioned from an active pressing trigger to a rest-defence mechanism, enhancing compactness and minimizing high turnovers (from 5 to 0), which improved ball retention in deep areas. Although Westport’s xG dropped from 0.34 to 0.24 and shots decreased from 4 to 1, Kingsmoor FC’s expected goals against increased from 0 to 0.94, reflecting their exploitation of Westport’s deeper posture. The field tilt for Westport slightly improved (30.8% to 32.0%), but the slower tempo and reduced line height effectively disrupted Kingsmoor’s wide, crossing play and limited their attacking progression despite Kingsmoor’s increased box touches (from 1 to 2). This balance highlights Westport’s controlled transition to a conservative, counter-attacking structure while managing Kingsmoor’s vertical overloads [#1459].
